new_restaurants.label: New Restaurants
new_restaurants.title: New Restaurants (opened in the last 6 months)
new_restaurants.methodology: Ranked by local food-press buzz, opening recency, and ratings. Only includes places with a confirmed opening date within the last 6 months.

restaurants.name: Board & Brew
restaurants.blurb: The Del Mar original from 1979 lands in the new RaDD Building with waterfront patio seating, bartop views, and 12 beers on draft.

restaurants.name: By The Sea
restaurants.blurb: Black Swan Hospitality is bringing Mediterranean coastal cooking to Coronado, drawing on the Amalfi Coast, French Riviera, and Greek Isles. Reclaimed wood beams, imported cobblestones, and a sun-soaked patio near the Pacific.

restaurants.name: Verise
restaurants.blurb: Chef Riccardo Bilotta trained at two- and three-Michelin-starred kitchens in Tuscany and Spain, and that pedigree shows up in the menu at this Italian spot inside Hotel Solea. Fresh pastas, wood-fired pizzas, and an aperitivo-leaning cocktail program with standouts like the Calabrian Marg and Olio Martini.

restaurants.name: Tierra y Mar
restaurants.blurb: Chef Bryan Texis roots the menu in Baja California and Mexican regional tradition – beef birria, Camarones al Diablo, Pescado a la Talla – inside a $10.7 million room that blends Cycladic and Moorish design with handcrafted wood beams and mosaic tile. The bar runs 35-plus tequilas and mezcals. An’s Gelato Gate D5 – Oceanside – An’s Gelato’s next concept takes over the historic Top Gun House at Mis

restaurants.name: The Polished Pigeon
restaurants.blurb: A sober gathering space built around community and connection, designed for those in recovery, the sober-curious, and anyone after a social environment that doesn’t revolve around alcohol.

restaurants.name: Sun Gold Point
restaurants.blurb: A family diner built around locally sourced ingredients, clean cooking, and no seed oils. Still in soft launch, but already getting attention.

restaurants.name: Copper Kings Burgers
restaurants.blurb: Copper Kings Burgers is bringing its cult-favorite smashburgers to Oceanside, returning to its coastal roots with a bigger space and expanded menu. Known for house-made milk buns, creative toppings, and scratch-made everything, this North County favorite blends comfort food with serious attention to detail.

restaurants.name: Rei do Gado
restaurants.blurb: The Brazilian churrascaria that’s been a Gaslamp fixture since 1999 returns after nearly two years with a full interior refresh from designer Rachel Larraine Crawford of Tiger Veil. The original butterfly artwork stays; everything around it got a refresh with natural materials and Brazil-inspired tropical touches. Telefèric Barcelona  –  La Jolla – This family-owned Barcelona original, 30-plus yea

restaurants.name: Sugarfish
restaurants.blurb: Renown Los Angeles sushi brand Sugarfish is finally making its long-anticipated San Diego debut in spring 2026, bringing Chef Kazunori Nozawa’s famed “Trust Me” omakase-style menus - built around pristine fish, warm rice, and crisp nori - to a 40-seat, design-forward space inside the new 2100 Kettner development, where architect Robert Tsurimoto Kirsten has crafted a serene, ocean-inspired setting

restaurants.name: Zuma
restaurants.blurb: San Diego’s first California location of the global luxury Japanese chain. This is the one the fine-dining crowd is waiting for.

restaurants.name: CHAGEE Modern Teahouse
restaurants.blurb: The brand’s first San Diego location opens at Westfield UTC as the first pet-friendly CHAGEE in the country. The summer menu features Citrus Teafreshers with hand-muddled citrus, and yes, there’s a Puptea for the dogs on the patio.

restaurants.name: SunLife Organics
restaurants.blurb: The wellness smoothie brand’s newest outpost is a custom Airstream parked directly on Del Beach at Hotel del Coronado, open to guests and the public. The full lineup is here – Million Dollar Smoothie, signature bowls, the Garden Matcha – plus two Del exclusives worth trying: The Victorian and the Hotel Del Bowl.

restaurants.name: Queenstown
restaurants.blurb: New Zealand-influenced comfort food and cocktails on Camino Del Mar from the team behind Bare Back Grill and Raglan Public House. The glass pavilion with ocean views and indoor-outdoor seating is the detail worth watching for.

restaurants.name: Pastaria Vivi
restaurants.blurb: Pastaria Vivi brings a fresh take on Italian dining to Encinitas, blending handmade pasta, a retail shop, and casual dining. With 75+ rotating combinations, curated wines, and classes, it’s a go-to spot for both dining in and cooking at home. Opens April 11.

restaurants.name: Georgette’s
restaurants.blurb: An intimate cocktail bar upstairs at À L’ouest from TRUST Restaurant Group. Travel-themed, moody, and reservation-driven. Expect 90-minute table bookings with open seating at the bar.
